audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Nazareth rejection, sending the Twelve, Herod/John narrative, feeding five thousand, sea-walking, and Gennesaret healings.

verses.restored: He went out from there and came into his homeland, and his disciples followed him.

familiar.text: And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

modern.text: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ ⸀ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing were struck with wonder, saying, From where are these things to this one? What is this wisdom given to him, and such powers coming through his hands?

familiar.text: And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?

modern.text: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?

original.text: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο ⸂διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ⸃· καὶ ⸀οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα, καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα ⸀τούτῳ, καὶ ⸀αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ⸀γινόμεναι;

verses.restored: Is this not the craftsman, the son of Mary, brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Are not his sisters here with us? And they stumbled over him.

familiar.text: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.

modern.text: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.

original.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων, ὁ υἱὸς ⸀τῆς Μαρίας ⸂καὶ ἀδελφὸς⸃ Ἰακώβου καὶ ⸀Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος; καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honor except in his homeland, among his relatives, and in his house.

familiar.text: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἔλεγεν⸃ αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς ⸂συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He was not able to do any power there, except that he laid hands on a few sick people and healed them.

familiar.text: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.

modern.text: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ⸂ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν⸃, εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν·

verses.restored: He marveled because of their lack of trust. He went around the villages in a circle, teaching.

familiar.text: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.

modern.text: And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people. The Ministry of the Twelve (Matthew 10:5–15; Luke 9:1–6)

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν. Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων.

verses.restored: He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.

familiar.text: And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;

modern.text: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.

original.text: καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο, καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων,

verses.restored: He instructed them to take nothing for the way except a staff: no bread, no bag, no copper in the belt,

familiar.text: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:

modern.text: He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey—no bread, no bag, no money in their belts—

original.text: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον, μὴ ⸂ἄρτον, μὴ πήραν⸃, μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν,

verses.restored: but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics.

familiar.text: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.

modern.text: and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια, καὶ μὴ ⸀ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας.

verses.restored: He said to them, Wherever you enter a house, remain there until you go out from there.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.

modern.text: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου ⸀ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν, ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν.

verses.restored: Whatever place does not receive you or hear you, as you go out from there, shake the dust from under your feet as a testimony to them.

familiar.text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

modern.text: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”

original.text: καὶ ⸂ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται⸃ ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν, ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον ⸀αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: They went out and proclaimed that people should turn/realign.

familiar.text: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.

modern.text: So they set out and preached that the people should repent.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ⸀ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα ⸀μετανοῶσιν,

verses.restored: They cast out many unclean spirits, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.

familiar.text: And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.

modern.text: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil. The Beheading of John (Matthew 14:1–12; Luke 9:7–9)

original.text: καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον, καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον.

verses.restored: King Herod heard, for Jesus' name had become known. Some were saying, John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him.

familiar.text: And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

modern.text: Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”

original.text: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης, φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸀ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ⸂ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν⸃, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ·

verses.restored: Others were saying, He is Elijah. Others were saying, A prophet like one of the prophets.

familiar.text: Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.

modern.text: Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”

original.text: ἄλλοι ⸀δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι ⸀προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.

verses.restored: But Herod, hearing, said, John, whom I beheaded, has been raised.

familiar.text: But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.

modern.text: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ⸀ὁ Ἡρῴδης ⸀ἔλεγεν· Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην, οὗτος ⸀ἠγέρθη.

verses.restored: For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her.

familiar.text: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.

modern.text: For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound and imprisoned, on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.

original.text: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν·

verses.restored: For John had been saying to Herod, It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.

familiar.text: For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.

modern.text: For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”

original.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.

verses.restored: Herodias held it against him and wanted to kill him, but she was not able.

familiar.text: Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:

modern.text: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she had been unable,

original.text: ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο·

verses.restored: For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and protected him. Hearing him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he heard him gladly.

familiar.text: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.

modern.text: because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. When he heard John’s words, he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην, εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον, καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ⸀ἠπόρει, καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν.

verses.restored: An opportune day came when Herod, on his birthday, made a banquet for his nobles, military commanders, and the first people of Galilee.

familiar.text: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;

modern.text: On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.

original.text: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ⸀ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας,

verses.restored: When Herodias' daughter came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining with him. The king said to the girl, Ask me whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.

familiar.text: And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.

modern.text: When the daughter of Herodias came and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests, and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”

original.text: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς ⸂αὐτῆς τῆς⸃ Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης ⸂καὶ ἀρεσάσης⸃ τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις, ⸂εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς⸃ τῷ κορασίῳ· Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς, καὶ δώσω σοι·

verses.restored: He swore to her, Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half my reign.

familiar.text: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.

modern.text: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”

original.text: καὶ ὤμοσεν ⸀αὐτῇ· ⸂Ὅ τι⸃ ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου.

verses.restored: She went out and said to her mother, What should I ask? She said, The head of John the Baptist.

familiar.text: And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.

modern.text: Then she went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?” And her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς· Τί ⸀αἰτήσωμαι; ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ ⸀βαπτίζοντος.

verses.restored: Immediately she came in with haste to the king and asked, saying, I want you to give me at once the head of John the Baptist on a platter.

familiar.text: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.

modern.text: At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”

original.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα ⸀εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα· Θέλω ἵνα ⸂ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι⸃ ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.

verses.restored: The king became deeply grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him, he did not want to refuse her.

familiar.text: And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.

modern.text: The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.

original.text: καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ⸀ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ⸂ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν⸃·

verses.restored: Immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded him to bring John's head. He went and beheaded him in the prison.

familiar.text: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

modern.text: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ⸀ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ. ⸀καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ

verses.restored: He brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

familiar.text: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.

modern.text: The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.

original.text: καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: When his disciples heard, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.

familiar.text: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

modern.text: When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Matthew 14:13–21; Luke 9:10–17; John 6:1–15)

original.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ.

verses.restored: The apostles gathered to Jesus and reported to him all they had done and taught.

familiar.text: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.

modern.text: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.

original.text: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ ⸀πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν.

verses.restored: He said to them, Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little. For many were coming and going, and they had no opportunity even to eat.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

modern.text: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

original.text: καὶ ⸀λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατʼ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ⸀ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον. ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί, καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν.

verses.restored: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.

familiar.text: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.

modern.text: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.

original.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθον ⸂ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον⸃ κατʼ ἰδίαν.

verses.restored: Many saw them going and recognized them; on foot from all the cities they ran together there and arrived ahead of them.

familiar.text: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.

modern.text: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.

original.text: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ⸀ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί, καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον ⸀αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Coming out, he saw a great crowd and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.

familiar.text: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.

modern.text: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ⸀εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα, καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά.

verses.restored: When it was already a late hour, his disciples came to him and said, This place is deserted, and the hour is already late.

familiar.text: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:

modern.text: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.

original.text: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος, καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή·

verses.restored: Release them so they may go into the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat.

familiar.text: Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.

modern.text: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”

original.text: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς ⸂τί φάγωσιν⸃.

verses.restored: But he answered, You give them something to eat. They said, Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii of bread and give them to eat?

familiar.text: He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?

modern.text: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν. καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν δηναρίων διακοσίων ἄρτους καὶ ⸀δώσομεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν;

verses.restored: He said to them, How many loaves do you have? Go see. Knowing, they said, Five, and two fish.

familiar.text: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.

modern.text: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five—and two fish.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πόσους ⸂ἔχετε ἄρτους⸃; ⸀ὑπάγετε ἴδετε. καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν· Πέντε, καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.

verses.restored: He instructed them to make all recline in groups on the green grass.

familiar.text: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.

modern.text: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.

original.text: καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς ⸀ἀνακλῖναι πάντας συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ.

verses.restored: They reclined in groups of hundreds and fifties.

familiar.text: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

modern.text: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.

original.text: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ ⸀κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ ⸁κατὰ πεντήκοντα.

verses.restored: Taking the five loaves and two fish, looking up to heaven, he blessed, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples to set before them; and he divided the two fish among all.

familiar.text: And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.

modern.text: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.

original.text: καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς ⸀αὐτοῦ ἵνα ⸀παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: All ate and were filled.

familiar.text: And they did all eat, and were filled.

modern.text: They all ate and were satisfied,

original.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν·

verses.restored: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and of the fish.

familiar.text: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.

modern.text: and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.

original.text: καὶ ἦραν ⸂κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα⸃ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων.

verses.restored: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.

familiar.text: And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.

modern.text: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves. Jesus Walks on Water (Matthew 14:22–33; John 6:16–21)

original.text: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες ⸂τοὺς ἄρτους⸃ πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες.

verses.restored: Immediately he compelled his disciples to enter the boat and go before him to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while he released the crowd.

familiar.text: And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.

modern.text: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν ⸂εἰς τὸ πέραν⸃ πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν, ἕως αὐτὸς ⸀ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον.

verses.restored: After taking leave of them, he went away into the mountain to pray.

familiar.text: And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.

modern.text: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.

original.text: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

verses.restored: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

familiar.text: And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

modern.text: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.

original.text: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

verses.restored: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he intended to pass by them.

familiar.text: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.

modern.text: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν, ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος ⸀αὐτοῖς, περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Seeing him walking on the sea, they thought he was a ghost/appearance and cried out.

familiar.text: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:

modern.text: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost—

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ⸂ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα⸃ ἔδοξαν ⸂ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν⸃ καὶ ἀνέκραξαν,

verses.restored: For they all saw him and were troubled. Immediately he spoke with them and said, Take courage; I am. Do not fear.

familiar.text: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.

modern.text: for they all saw Him and were terrified. But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”

original.text: πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν. ⸂ὁ δὲ εὐθὺς⸃ ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

verses.restored: He went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased. They were exceedingly astonished in themselves.

familiar.text: And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.

modern.text: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded,

original.text: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος. καὶ λίαν ⸂ἐκ περισσοῦ⸃ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ⸀ἐξίσταντο,

verses.restored: For they did not understand about the loaves, but their heart had been hardened.

familiar.text: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.

modern.text: for they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts had been hardened. Jesus Heals at Gennesaret (Matthew 14:34–36)

original.text: οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις, ⸂ἀλλʼ ἦν⸃ αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη.

verses.restored: Crossing over, they came to land at Gennesaret and anchored.

familiar.text: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.

modern.text: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and moored the boat.

original.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ⸂ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς⸃ Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν.

verses.restored: When they came out of the boat, immediately people recognized him.

familiar.text: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,

modern.text: As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ⸀εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν

verses.restored: They ran around that whole region and began to carry the sick on mats to wherever they heard he was.

familiar.text: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

modern.text: and ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.

original.text: ⸂περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ⸃ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ⸀ὅτι ἐστίν.

verses.restored: Wherever he entered villages, cities, or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and pleaded that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched it were saved/healed.

familiar.text: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.

modern.text: And wherever He went—villages and towns and countrysides—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.

original.text: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ ⸂εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς⸃ ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ⸀ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ⸀ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο.
